q: Which of the following is NOT one of the five phases listed under Design-Build Services by Administration (Sec. 2.1.1 - 2.1.5)?
o: Schematic Design Phase
Contract Document Phase
Post-Construction Phase
Design Development Phase
n: The five listed phases are Project Definition, Schematic Design, Design Development, Contract Document, and Construction Phase — there is no separate Post-Construction Phase under this scope. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 2.1.1-2.1.5)

q: Using the scenario figures, what is the guaranteed maximum project construction cost ceiling (estimated cost plus the 10% allowance) under Sec. 2.2.3?
n: PHP 10,000,000 estimated cost + 10% (PHP 1,000,000) = PHP 11,000,000, the ceiling beyond which Sec. 2.2.3 makes the Architect liable for the excess. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 2.2.3)
scenario: An Architect is engaged under Design-Build Services with a Guaranteed Maximum Project Construction Cost. The estimated project construction cost given to the Owner/Client is PHP 10,000,000. The Architect's Administration Fee for the project is PHP 500,000.

q: Per Sec. 2.1.5(h), the final listed expanded Construction Phase duty is management of what?
o: The Architect's personal finances
The Owner/Client's marketing campaign
Design competition prize funds
All other business transactions related to the project construction/implementation
n: Item (h) covers management of all other business transactions related to the project construction/implementation, as a catch-all duty. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 2.1.5(h))

q: Per Sec. 4.3, subject to the Owner/Client's approval, which support personnel may the Architect appoint aside from the usual labor personnel required?
o: A Professional Advisor and a Competition Secretariat
A separate licensed Architect of record and a design competition Jury
A construction superintendent, purchasing agent, timekeeper and property clerk
An independent financial auditor and a government building official
n: Sec. 4.3 lists a construction superintendent, purchasing agent, timekeeper and property clerk as personnel the Architect may appoint, subject to Owner/Client approval. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 4.3)

q: Per Sec. 2.1.5(g), the Architect negotiates with which parties regarding jurisdiction over the project?
o: Only the local homeowners' association
The Integrated and Accredited Professional Organization of Architects (IAPOA) exclusively
Government and private agencies having jurisdiction over the project
Competing Architects bidding for the same project
n: Item (g) lists negotiation with Government and private agencies having jurisdiction over the project. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 2.1.5(g))

q: Per Sec. 1.2, the several project delivery methods devised by the building industry and the architectural profession share what ultimate goal?
o: Eliminating the need for construction permits
Maximizing the Architect's professional fee on every project
Transferring all project risk to the Owner/Client
Handling projects in the shortest possible time, at the lowest possible cost, and at acceptable quality and performance
n: Sec. 1.2 describes the goal as handling projects in the shortest possible time, at the lowest possible cost, and at an acceptable quality and performance. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 1.2)

q: Per Sec. 3.2.1, regardless of which arrangement he adopts under Sec. 3.1, what must the Architect strictly retain?
o: His right to waive professional liability for construction defects
His separate/distinct professional identity, prerogatives and integrity as an Architect
Exclusive control over the Owner/Client's financing arrangements
A separate corporate entity registered with the SEC
n: Sec. 3.2.1 requires the Architect to retain his separate/distinct professional identity, prerogatives and integrity as an Architect. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 3.2.1)

q: Per Sec. 3.1, an Architect who wishes to be involved in construction (including of his own design) other than through the usual bidding-out process or the modes of Design-Build Services may adopt which arrangement?
o: Only forming a joint venture with the project's Owner/Client
Automatically forfeiting his design fee to the contractor
Delegating all construction supervision to an unrelated third-party consultant
Being part of, or a member of, the entity constructing his design, or being himself a State-licensed contractor implementing the design
n: Sec. 3.1.1 allows the Architect to be part of or a member of the entity constructing his design, and Sec. 3.1.2 allows him to be himself a State-licensed contractor implementing his design (or that of others). (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 3.1.1-3.1.2)

q: Per Sec. 1.4, Design-Build Services simplifies and expedites the process of project delivery while providing what kind of solutions?
o: Government-mandated standard solutions
Creative, cost-effective solutions
Purely aesthetic solutions
Solutions limited to residential projects only
n: Sec. 1.4 states that Design-Build Services simplifies and expedites project delivery while providing creative cost-effective solutions. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 1.4)

q: Using the scenario figures, the actual project construction cost comes in at PHP 11,300,000 (i.e., PHP 300,000 above the guaranteed maximum of PHP 11,000,000), with no legitimate CVOs/EWOs or certified escalation involved. How much of the excess is the Architect liable for under Sec. 2.2.3?
o: Nothing — the Owner/Client absorbs any excess automatically
PHP 500,000 flat, regardless of the actual excess amount
PHP 1,300,000, the full actual cost above the original estimate
PHP 300,000, since it is less than his PHP 500,000 Administration Fee
n: Sec. 2.2.3 makes the Architect liable for the excess amount over the guaranteed maximum, but only up to the amount of his Administration Fee. Here the excess (PHP 300,000) is less than the PHP 500,000 fee, so the Architect is liable for the full PHP 300,000 excess. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 2.2.3)
scenario: An Architect is engaged under Design-Build Services with a Guaranteed Maximum Project Construction Cost. The estimated project construction cost given to the Owner/Client is PHP 10,000,000. The Architect's Administration Fee for the project is PHP 500,000.

q: Per Sec. 2.2.4, additional expenditures beyond the guaranteed maximum project construction cost that are due to legitimate change/variation orders (CVOs), extra work orders (EWOs), or certified substantial escalation of material/labor costs are borne by whom?
o: The piecework contractors involved
The Owner/Client
The Architect, out of his Administration Fee
The Architect's professional liability insurer automatically
n: Sec. 2.2.4 provides that such additional costs, being due to causes not attributable to the Architect's fault, shall be borne by the Owner/Client. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 2.2.4)

q: An Architect performing Design-Build Services holds a personal business investment in a supplier used on the project, creating a potential conflict of interest. Per the Architects Credo referenced in Sec. 3.2.2, what is he pledged to do?
o: Automatically divest from the investment before accepting the project
Keep the investment confidential unless a court subpoenas the information
Disclose the investment whenever required, and ensure it neither compromises the Client's legitimate interest nor interferes with his duty to render impartial judgment
Transfer the investment's profits directly to the Client as compensation
n: Sec. 3.2.2 quotes the Architects Credo pledge to disclose whenever required any business investment or venture that may create a conflict of interest, ensuring it neither compromises the Client's legitimate interest nor interferes with the duty to render impartial judgment. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 3.2.2 / Architects Credo)

q: Which of the following is listed among the Architect's expanded Construction Phase duties under Design-Build Services by Administration?
o: Issuing the Certificate of Occupancy on behalf of the building official
Sitting as Professional Advisor to a design competition Jury
Organization and hiring of construction personnel, and designation of duties and remunerations
Approving the Architect's own guaranteed maximum cost estimate
n: Item (b) of Sec. 2.1.5 lists organization and hiring of construction personnel, and designation of duties and remunerations, as an expanded Construction Phase duty. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 2.1.5(b))

q: Per Sec. 2.1, the scope of Design-Build Services by Administration is similar to the scope of the Architect's Regular Design Services found in which SPP Document?
o: SPP Document 206
SPP Document 203
SPP Document 201
SPP Document 202
n: Sec. 2.1 states the scope of Design-Build Services by Administration is similar to that of the Architect's Regular Design Services under SPP Document 202. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 2.1)

q: Per Sec. 4.1, the manner of payment to the Architect under Design-Build Services follows what?
o: Completion of the entire project in a single lump sum
The Architect's original design fee schedule only
A fixed monthly retainer regardless of progress
The progress of construction
n: Sec. 4.1 states the manner of payment to the Architect follows the progress of construction. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 4.1)

q: Using the scenario figures, suppose the actual project construction cost instead reaches PHP 12,500,000 (PHP 1,500,000 above the guaranteed maximum of PHP 11,000,000), with no legitimate CVOs/EWOs or certified escalation involved. Under Sec. 2.2.3, how much of that excess must the Architect bear?
o: PHP 500,000 — capped at the amount of his Administration Fee
Nothing, since the excess exceeds his control
PHP 1,000,000, being 10% of the estimated cost
The full PHP 1,500,000 excess
n: Sec. 2.2.3 caps the Architect's liability for the excess at the amount of his Administration Fee. Even though the actual excess is PHP 1,500,000, the Architect is liable only up to his PHP 500,000 Administration Fee. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 2.2.3)
scenario: An Architect is engaged under Design-Build Services with a Guaranteed Maximum Project Construction Cost. The estimated project construction cost given to the Owner/Client is PHP 10,000,000. The Architect's Administration Fee for the project is PHP 500,000.

q: An Architect is himself a State-licensed contractor and personally implements a design (his own or another's). Which provision of SPP Document 207 covers this specific arrangement?
o: Sec. 4.3
n: Sec. 3.1.2 specifically covers the Architect being himself a State-licensed contractor implementing his design or that of others. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 3.1.2)

q: Per Sec. 4.3, salaries of the construction superintendent, purchasing agent, timekeeper and property clerk are paid by whom, and are they deductible from the Architect's Fee?
o: Paid by the Architect, and fully deductible from the Architect's Fee
Paid by the Owner/Client, but deducted from the Architect's Fee at year-end
Split equally between the Architect and the Owner/Client
Paid by the Owner/Client, and NOT deductible from the Architect's Fee
n: Sec. 4.3 states these salaries are paid by the Owner/Client and are not deductible from the Architect's Fee under this SPP. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 4.3)

q: Per Sec. 4.2, who shall pay for the cost of all permits, licenses and other incidentals to the work?
o: The Architect
The Owner/Client
The construction superintendent
The piecework contractors, equally shared
n: Sec. 4.2 states the Owner/Client shall pay for the cost of all permits, licenses and other incidentals to the work. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 4.2)

q: Per Sec. 4.1, who directly pays all costs for labor and materials, with the Architect not advancing any money for such expenditures?
o: The Client
The Architect
The IAPOA
The piecework contractors
n: Sec. 4.1 states the Client directly pays all costs for labor and materials, and the Architect does not advance any money for payment of related expenditures. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 4.1)

q: What is the defining liability feature of Design-Build Services described in Sec. 1.5, distinguishing it from the Architect's regular design services?
o: The Owner/Client assumes all liability once construction begins
The Architect is liable only for the design, never for construction
The Architect assumes professional responsibility and civil liability for both the design and the construction of the project
Liability is shared equally with the general contractor by default
n: Sec. 1.5 provides that in Design-Build Services the Architect assumes professional responsibility and civil liability for both the design and the construction of the project. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 1.5)

q: Under Sec. 2.2.3, the Architect's guarantee on the project construction cost is that the actual cost will not exceed the estimated cost by more than what percentage?
o: Twenty percent (20%)
Five percent (5%)
Ten percent (10%)
Fifteen percent (15%)
n: Sec. 2.2.3 states the project construction cost is guaranteed by the Architect not to exceed Ten Percent (10%) of the estimated project construction cost. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 2.2.3)
scenario: An Architect is engaged under Design-Build Services with a Guaranteed Maximum Project Construction Cost. The estimated project construction cost given to the Owner/Client is PHP 10,000,000. The Architect's Administration Fee for the project is PHP 500,000.

q: Using the scenario figures, the project is actually completed for PHP 9,200,000. How much of the resulting savings, if any, is due to the Architect under Sec. 2.2.2?
o: PHP 0 — savings belong solely to the Owner
n: The savings is PHP 10,000,000 − PHP 9,200,000 = PHP 800,000. Sec. 2.2.2 divides this equally between Owner/Client and Architect, giving the Architect PHP 400,000. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 2.2.2)
scenario: An Architect is engaged under Design-Build Services with a Guaranteed Maximum Project Construction Cost. The estimated project construction cost given to the Owner/Client is PHP 10,000,000. The Architect's Administration Fee for the project is PHP 500,000.

q: SPP Document 207 on Design-Build Services replaces which earlier document?
o: The 1979 UAP Doc. 202
The 2000 UAP Doc. 207
SPP Document 206
The 1979 UAP Doc. 207
n: The header of SPP Document 207 states it replaces the 1979 UAP Doc. 207. (Source: SPP Document 207, title page note)

q: Per Sec. 3.2.1, in adopting any construction-involvement arrangement, the Architect remains subject to the standards and tenets of the SPP, particularly which two documents?
o: SPP Document 204-A and SPP Document 204-B
SPP Document 201 and SPP Document 208
SPP Document 200 (Code of Ethical Conduct) and SPP Document 202
SPP Document 203 and SPP Document 205
n: Sec. 3.2.1 names SPP Document 200, the Code of Ethical Conduct, and SPP Document 202 as the standards the Architect remains subject to. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 3.2.1)

q: If, upon completion of a Guaranteed Maximum Cost project, the actual project construction cost is lower than the estimated cost, how is the resulting savings handled?
o: The full savings is retained by the Architect alone
The savings is forfeited to the general contractor
The full savings is retained by the Owner/Client alone
The savings is divided equally between the Owner/Client and the Architect
n: Sec. 2.2.2 provides that if there is realized savings from the estimated project construction cost, it is divided equally between the Owner/Client and the Architect. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 2.2.2)
scenario: An Architect is engaged under Design-Build Services with a Guaranteed Maximum Project Construction Cost. The estimated project construction cost given to the Owner/Client is PHP 10,000,000. The Architect's Administration Fee for the project is PHP 500,000.

q: What distinguishes Design-Build Services with a Guaranteed Maximum Project Construction Cost (Sec. 2.2) from Design-Build Services by Administration (Sec. 2.1)?
o: The Architect no longer performs any design services at all
The Architect provides the Owner/Client a guaranteed maximum project construction cost for the project
The Owner/Client is barred from receiving any share of cost savings
The five design phases under Sec. 2.1 are eliminated entirely
n: Sec. 2.2.1 states this method is essentially the same as Design-Build Services by Administration, except the Architect provides a guaranteed maximum project construction cost. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 2.2.1)

q: Per Sec. 2.1.5(d), what does the Architect procure during the expanded Construction Phase?
o: Design competition entries for jury review
Materials, plants and equipment, licenses and permits
Insurance policies for the Owner/Client's other properties
Only office supplies for the site office
n: Item (d) lists procurement of materials, plants and equipment, licenses and permits. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 2.1.5(d))

q: Under Design-Build Services by Administration, when do the Architect's Construction Phase duties go beyond periodic inspection and assessment?
o: When the various phases of design services are completed
Only when the Owner/Client specifically requests it in writing
Only for projects exceeding a certain floor area
Never — periodic inspection remains the limit of Construction Phase duties
n: Sec. 2.1.5 states that once the various phases of design services are completed, the Construction Phase goes beyond periodic inspection and assessment to include additional duties (items a-h). (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 2.1.5)

q: Per Sec. 4.1, what financial mechanism is generally given to the Architect beforehand, to be accounted for and subject to periodic auditing by the Client?
o: A performance bond
An irrevocable letter of credit
A revolving fund
A design competition prize fund
n: Sec. 4.1 provides that a revolving fund is generally given to the Architect beforehand, accounted for and subject to periodic auditing by the Client. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 4.1)

q: An Architect negotiates and enters into a contract with a piecework contractor and evaluates the contractor's work accomplishments. Which expanded Construction Phase duty covers this?
o: Item (g) — negotiation with Government and private agencies having jurisdiction over the project
Item (a) — preparation of schedule of work, estimates of materials, labor, transportation, equipment and services
Item (h) — management of all other business transactions related to the project
Item (c) — negotiation and entering into contract with piecework contractors and evaluation of work accomplishments
n: Item (c) specifically covers negotiating and entering into contracts with piecework contractors and evaluating work accomplishments. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 2.1.5(c))

q: Per Sec. 4.4, the method of compensation under Design-Build Services may be modified by using relevant alternatives detailed in which SPP Document?
o: SPP Document 205
SPP Document 208
SPP Document 202
SPP Document 201
n: Sec. 4.4 states the method of compensation may be modified by using the relevant alternatives detailed in SPP Doc. 202. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 4.4)

q: Per Sec. 2.1.5(f), among the expanded Construction Phase duties, the Architect is responsible for keeping what?
o: A public bidding registry
Records and books of accounts
The minutes of the Jury's deliberations
The Owner/Client's personal tax records
n: Item (f) lists keeping records and books of accounts as an expanded Construction Phase duty. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 2.1.5(f))

q: Per Sec. 2.2.4, which nationally recognized agency is cited as an example of a body that may certify substantial escalation of the costs of materials or labor?
o: The Department of Trade and Industry (DTI)
The National Economic Development Authority (NEDA)
The Integrated and Accredited Professional Organization of Architects (IAPOA)
The Professional Regulatory Board of Architecture (PRBoA)
n: Sec. 2.2.4 cites the National Economic Development Authority (NEDA) as an example of a nationally recognized agency that may certify such data. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 2.2.4)

q: According to Sec. 1.3, what qualifies an Architect to take a direct role in a project from conceptualization to implementation?
o: His education, training and expertise
His membership in the Jury of design competitions
His seniority among other Architects on the project
A special contractor's license issued by the IAPOA
n: Sec. 1.3 attributes this qualification to the Architect's education, training and expertise. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 1.3)

q: Per Sec. 2.2.4, "CVOs" and "EWOs" refer to what?
o: Contractor verification orders and equipment withdrawal orders
Change/variation orders and extra work orders
Cost variance offsets and emergency work orders
Certified valuation orders and estimated work outlays
n: Sec. 2.2.4 uses CVOs to mean change/variation orders and EWOs to mean extra work orders. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 2.2.4)

q: Per Sec. 1.1, what three elements does a building project need to balance, which Design-Build Services can best achieve?
o: Time, quality and cost
Time, safety and profit
Design, permits and labor
Cost, materials and manpower
n: Sec. 1.1 states the need to balance time, quality and cost, which in many cases is best achieved through Design-Build Services. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 1.1)
